discrepancies.discrepancy: The migration README, accepted architecture, and M0 dispatch record different inspected baselines.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: M0 output identity is the dispatch sourceRevision 396f427009ade1a4243188c7da75ff335efe9e82. Historical baseline strings remain provenance only and cannot validate an M0 or later implementation packet.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Every M0 output carries baselineCommit and sourceRevision equal to the dispatch sourceRevision.

discrepancies.discrepancy: The current audit plan makes blueprint-packet an inventory-stage prerequisite, so an unavailable Membrane packet makes the run incomplete before providers can reconcile.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Blueprint becomes optional typed context evidence. Audit runs every applicable non-Blueprint provider, preserves the selected-provider denominator, emits visible structural-coverage limits and a recommendation, and returns typed provider-level degradation only for an explicitly Blueprint-dependent operation.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Blueprint-absent qualification proves applicable providers still reconcile and no unrelated provider reports a machinery crash or empty success.

discrepancies.discrepancy: Current shipped product algorithms are implemented in Node and Python modules, including orchestration, provider execution, Audit, Research, review, receipts, and policy integrations.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Port Legion-owned shipped algorithms to the shared Rust runtime. Preserve Node/Python only when the refreshed executable inventory proves a path is development-only or an intentional external project tool; no native runtime may invoke Node, Python, shell scripts, or another Legion runtime for Legion semantics.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Installed-product qualification finds no Node/Python runtime dependency for Legion-owned behavior and retains classified development tooling.

discrepancies.discrepancy: Current provider records mix runtime scripts, legacy named checks, reasoning contracts, imported artifacts, and Blueprint consumption without one target-owner taxonomy.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: The frozen provider boundary assigns every current registry provider a target semantic owner: Rust algorithm, typed external project tool, or host service; declarative rules remain assets and Blueprint remains optional typed evidence rather than a provider-runtime owner.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: provider-boundary.json has no unclassified registry row and the M5 gate rejects unknown provider owners.

discrepancies.discrepancy: Current external-process execution has an allowlist and receipts, but the native target has not yet made its typed request, immediate policy evaluation, bounded execution, and receipt contract the sole implementation path.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: All external executable use is a typed, bounded external-project-tool effect evaluated by Arcane immediately before execution and accompanied by an effect receipt. Shell command strings, unsealed executable bytes, missing process-tree control, missing immutable output, and unapproved destructive effects fail closed.
discrepancies.owner: M4 policy/receipt migration and M5 external-tool boundary
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Adversarial effect tests prove denial, timeout, output limit, cancellation, executable identity mismatch, and destructive-effect approval paths are receipt-backed.

discrepancies.discrepancy: Current host adapters are source-language implementation surfaces rather than a frozen native product adapter contract.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Host/client shims remain mechanical: detection, registration, paths, lifecycle projection, verification, repair, and cleanup only. Legion Rust owns routing, Audit, Research, Arcane evaluation, work graphs, receipts, and capability semantics; host trust and prompt policy remain host-owned.
discrepancies.owner: M2 client integration and M3 setup lifecycle
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Adapter conformance proves no adapter contains Legion semantic implementation and every claimed host surface has measured fidelity evidence.

discrepancies.discrepancy: Current legion state snapshot|verify is a mechanical test-state boundary and does not define production state roots, schema compatibility, leases, migration, rollback, interrupted recovery, or verified purge.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Implement only the frozen native state contract: Legion-owned platform user-data roots, version metadata, exclusive migration/setup lock, active-runtime leases, snapshot-plus-atomic-restore rollback, fail-closed recovery, and explicit verified purge. Keep snapshot|verify as development-only tooling.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: N-1 to N, interruption, N to N-1, corruption, concurrent clients, uninstall/reinstall, and purge scenarios satisfy state-contract.json.

discrepancies.discrepancy: The current source has no native installed-release binding that jointly verifies runtime provenance, version, catalog, MCP schema, and declarative assets before tool exposure.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Freeze and implement a release-binding contract in the distribution lane. Mismatch fails closed with exact repair; bounded package-update skew is repaired transactionally and never executes a mixed release.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Installed artifact tests cover stale assets, release mismatch, update repair, and old-runtime lease closure before incompatible migration.

discrepancies.discrepancy: Current review packets and completion semantics are spread across source-language modules and doctrine rather than one native runtime contract.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Rust owns deterministic review and completion protocols, while Oracle remains independent read-only Completion Validation. Completion Validation reconstructs raw scope, inspects source and consumers, and never reruns tests or authors a durable review artifact.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Completion validation and review contracts retain independence, unknown verdicts, source-first inspection, and no false clean behavior.

discrepancies.discrepancy: The migration could incorrectly absorb Membrane or Blueprint behavior while porting context consumers.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Membrane remains the typed context-selection and evidence-publication owner; Blueprint remains repository truth. Legion ports only the typed consumer boundary and does not modify Membrane, walk Blueprint storage, synthesize a local graph fallback, or transfer host/model ownership into Legion.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: No downstream allowlist includes Membrane source, and Blueprint absence produces typed degradation rather than an ad-hoc local substitute.

discrepancies.discrepancy: Research evidence and claim binding exist in current Python/Node implementations but have no native boundary contract yet.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Rust owns Research routing, evidence-ledger and claim-proof algorithms. Evidence remains opened-source and locator-bound; leads do not become evidence, unavailable required retrieval yields truthful UNPROVEN/typed degradation, and claims cannot exceed bound proof.
discrepancies.closureEvidence: Research qualification demonstrates evidence/claim linkage, uncertainty preservation, provider unavailability, and real external-source receipts.

discrepancies.discrepancy: A native runtime cutover could incorrectly delete Node/Python test, build, qualification, or repository-maintenance tooling together with shipped product paths.
discrepancies.targetDisposition: Retain development-only Node/Python tools unless a refreshed ledger classifies a path for deletion. Each retained development path requires path-specific exclusion proof; no M0 contract authorizes product-runtime edits or tooling removal.
discrepancies.owner: M7 hard cut and M8 cleanup
discrepancies.closureEvidence: The refreshed executable ledger and production-entrypoint absence scan distinguish retained tooling from removed product runtime paths.

notes: This is a semantic disposition ledger, not evidence that product-runtime migration has been implemented.
M0 performs source inspection and contract generation only; no Cargo invocation, runtime port, Membrane change, commit, or push is authorized.
